PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

12.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Duarte presented an overview of the crime statistics from the past two weeks. Councilmember Rebollo expressed high praise for Sergeant Duarte's work and wanted to relay positive feedback from local businesses to her.

Councilmember Garcia also commended Sergeant Duarte's efforts and inquired about patrol arrangements for the upcoming Fourth of July. Sergeant Duarte confirmed that there will be 24-hour patrols during that time.

Councilmember Lainez raised a concern about the City of Commerce having higher crime rates compared to neighboring cities. In response, Sergeant Duarte explained that this is largely attributed to the presence of two large shopping malls in the City of Commerce. She mentioned plans to engage with Cotadel and Commerce Shopping Mall representatives to explore the possibility of installing automated license plate readers as a means to reduce crime.

Mayor Argumedo added that he had already requested a presentation and wanted to start discussions with the Beverly Hills Sheriff's Department to explore the implementation of any applicable measures in the City of Commerce.


PUBLIC COMMENT Marco Jimenez made a formal request to the City Council, urging them to consider allocating funds for Miss Commerce in the forthcoming year. In his recommendation, he emphasized his extensive experience and provided assurance that his services would be valuable in spearheading the event. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Mayor Argumedo made a request to discuss items #11 and #7. 

Item #7 - Acting Public Works Director Nila provided an overview of the staff report. Councilmember Garcia inquired about the turf's lifespan, warranty, and maintenance plans. Acting Director Nila responded that the project would include turf and drought-tolerant plants, with a one-year warranty on installation. Further discussion took place. 

Councilmember Rebollo moved, seconded by Councilmember Lainez, to adopt a Resolution approving the Plans and Specifications for the Civic Center Landscape Renovation and Demonstration Garden Project. They also awarded a Construction Contract to Green Giant Landscape, Inc. for the same project and authorized Construction Management and Inspection Services by Transtech Engineers, Inc. and Lost West as per their On-Call Professional Consulting Services Agreements. The motion was approved with a vote of:

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, and Mayor Argumedo (4)
Absent: Vice Mayor Altamirano (1)

Item #11 - Acting Public Works Director Nila explained that the project had been completed within the scope of work and contract, allowing the release of the 5% contingency. The completed aspects included bus hub stations, pavement, and striping.

Councilmember Garcia inquired about lighting, to which Acting Director Nila confirmed that lighting from Stevenson Steakhouse to Jillson had been completed. Councilmember Garcia also asked about the purpose of the kiosk, which Transportation Director McFerguson clarified as a means to inform passengers about bus schedules and upcoming events.

Councilmember Lainez moved, seconded by Councilmember Rebollo, to adopt a Resolution accepting the Eastern Avenue Transit Hub Project as complete, and authorize staff to file the Notice of Completion with the County Recorder's Office and release the 5% retention per contract provisions. The motion was approved with a vote of:

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, and Mayor Argumedo (4)
Absent: Vice Mayor Altamirano (1)

City Manager Cisneros provided an update, stating that progress had been made regarding the installation of a pool. However, additional information was still needed, and it would be presented at a later time.

Further discussion took place concerning the design of Bristow Park, and the roof repairs for Bristow park would be addressed after the design is approved for Bristow park.  



16.. Committee and Commission Appointments Councilmember Lainez appointed Maria De Los Angeles Barrera to Senior Citizens Commission. 

14.. Adoption of Annual Operating 2023/2024 Fiscal Year Budget  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Mireya Garcia 
Assistant City Manager Domic provided a summary of the staff report during the meeting. It was mentioned that the City Council was not required to make an immediate decision regarding the requested positions as listed. Instead, they were asked to approve a total of $63,962,083 for the City to move forward to next fiscal year. The discussion regarding the specific positions could take place at a later time during the budget workshop sessions. 

Councilmember Rebollo suggested approving certain position requests, particularly emphasizing the need for full-time street helper positions. Councilmember Lainez expressed agreement with this recommendation.

City Manager Cisneros requested that the City Council submit their questions so that the staff could prepare responses accordingly. Mayor Argumedo emphasized the importance of obtaining a breakdown of costs for any additional requested items, as it would enable the Council to make more informed decisions. Councilmember Garcia supported this view, suggesting that the Department Director should be capable of addressing questions and being familiar with their respective budgets.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Rebollo offered her condolences to the family of Petty Officer Christopher W. Minor, who passed away the previous week.

Councilmember Lainez also expressed his condolences to the Minor family. In addition, he shared his participation in a six-month fellowship program focused on Water Education for Latino Leaders. Through this program, he gained valuable insights into water-related issues and water rights. As part of his involvement, on Saturday, the 17th, he co-hosted a water workshop in Paramount, which featured several speakers. Finally, he extended his wishes for a Happy Fourth of July to everyone.

13.. Second Amendment to Agreement with Athens Services for Residential Refuse and Recycling Services  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Acting Public Works Director Nila presented an overview of the staff report, which was followed by a discussion. During the discussion, Mayor Argumedo raised concerns about the issues regarding trash pick-up citywide.

Gary Clifford, President of Athens, addressed the issue by explaining that the residential program includes bulky item pick-up. Residents are required to call and schedule a pick-up for their bulky items, as Athens cannot pick them up without prior notification. This is to ensure that the items are not intended for donation to the Salvation Army or other organizations. However, if staff or Councilmembers make a request, Athens will promptly pick up the items.

Regarding commercial areas, different refuse providers are responsible for the trash collection.

In response to these concerns, the Mayor proposed the formation of an ad hoc committee to refine the pick-up process and improve efficiency. The goal would be to minimize the time that items remain uncollected. The Mayor also suggested that the community be informed and reminded to schedule pick-ups for their items by calling.
